title: Rutherford focuses on offense, aiming for district title - NewsBreak
text: SPRINGFIELD, Fla. (WMBB) — Entering his third year at the helm, Rutherford head coach Albert Floyd isn’t calling this a rebuild, not anymore. “We have some young guys and young playmakers that are expected to make plays,” Floyd said. “They may be young when it comes to age and experience, but we’ve got some guys that can take the ball yard a little bit.” Youth may be on their side, but depth remains a concern for the Rams heading into the 2025 season. Still, Rutherord believes the starting group can hang with anyone. “We’re a small team, we don’t have a bunch of guys,” Senior defensive back and wide receiver Bray’lyn Hurd said. “I feel like we’ve got fewer heads than a lot of teams we’ll be up against. But at the end of the day, we’ve got to work harder, push harder, and just be better every step of the way.” Last fall, Rutherford lost five games by just one possession. A few more breaks their way, and they might’ve been a seven-win team. This offseason, the coaching staff put a strong emphasis on ensuring the offense isn’t the reason for any future defeats. “We want to stop people, but we want to score points,” Floyd said. “If you don’t score, you don’t win. So we’re going to cater a little more to the offensive side of the ball, make sure those guys get the plays they need, and we’ll make adjustments on defense when we need to.” The Rams return starting quarterback Jaleel Reed, who showed flashes of promise during his freshman campaign. He’ll have plenty of weapons around him, anticipating huge senior seasons from Khazion Rochelle and Bray’lyn Hurd. They will also have a revamped offensive line and a new offensive coordinator, Matt Knauss, to help elevate Reed’s game. “Getting Coach K was big,” Reed said. “He’s helped me a lot from December until now. He’s on me every play. Every time I mess up, he’s there to correct me. I feel a lot more confident in my ability.” This marks Rutherford’s second season competing in a district with Marianna, Bozeman and North Bay Haven. Floyd still sees Marianna as the team to beat, but believes the Rams are in a position to make a run. “You can’t jump from winning two games to being on Steve Hardin’s level,” Floyd said. “But you can go from two wins to four, then to six, win your district, and focus on progress.” Rutherford opens its preseason against Freeport on August 15. The Rams kick off the regular season with a road game at Mosley on Friday, August 22. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to mypanhandle.com.
